suppress.notes:
FALSE POSITIVE. Dependency-Check matches io.projectreactor.netty:reactor-netty-core to cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty by version number alone (1.2.18), and then attaches the entire Netty advisory history to it -- 64 CVEs per service, including CVE-2019-20444/20445 and the netty-codec-http request-smuggling family. The report itself marks the match as low confidence. reactor-netty is a separate Spring project artifact and is not the software those advisories describe.
Scoped to the reactor-netty-core jar by file path on purpose: the real io.netty:* jars it pulls in are NOT suppressed and must keep reporting. Those are pinned via <netty.version> in each pom (4.1.137.Final at the time of writing).
SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-31: only mas-api-gateway still ships reactor-netty. NDI never used its webflux starter at all (removed), and Quarrying-Lease now runs WebClient on JdkClientHttpConnector with spring-boot-starter-reactor-netty excluded, so the jar is gone from both. The gateway cannot follow them: Spring Cloud Gateway's WebSocketClient bean comes from NettyConfiguration, and without it the context fails to start outright (verified - filteringWebHandler -> websocketRoutingFilter -> no WebSocketClient bean). This rule is kept in the other repos as a safety net in case a webflux starter returns transitively; it currently matches nothing there, which is the intended state.

FALSE POSITIVE. CVE-2018-1258 is an authorization bypass affecting Spring Security 5.0.5 used together with Spring Framework 5.0.5, fixed in 5.0.6 in 2018. The NVD entry carries an open-ended version range, so Dependency-Check re-flags it against every later release indefinitely. Nothing in MAS runs an affected version -- the estate is on Spring Security 6.5.x (Boot 3.5) and 7.0.x (Boot 4.0).
Affects all nine backends: core, web, oauth2-resource-server and crypto jars.

NOT APPLICABLE / NO OSS FIX AVAILABLE. The full run of Spring Framework advisories published against spring-core 6.2.0 - 6.2.19 (the 2026-08-20 batch of two, plus the 2026-11 batch of eight). Every one of them lists its 6.2.x fix as 6.2.20, which VMware ships as "Enterprise Support Only" -- it is not on Maven Central. 6.2.19 (2026-06-08) is the last OSS release of the 6.2 line, as Spring Boot 3.5.16 (2026-06-25) is the last OSS Boot 3.5 release. The only OSS fix is Spring Framework 7.0.8.1 / 7.0.9, i.e. a Spring Boot 3.5 -> 4.0 major migration, tracked separately. mas-backend-report and mas-backend-geo already run Boot 4 (spring-core 7.0.9) and do NOT report any of these.
NVD scores several of these 9.8 / 9.1 CRITICAL; VMware's own advisories rate the same CVEs LOW or MEDIUM. The NVD numbers are scoring artifacts -- go by the vendor rating and by reachability, below.
Per-CVE reachability, all re-verified by grep across every backend in the estate on 2026-09-03 (all counts ZERO): CVE-2026-47890 SSE stream corruption with view fragments -- needs Spring MVC/WebFlux SSE + view fragments. No RouterFunction / ServerResponse.sse / SseEmitter / text/event-stream anywhere. CVE-2026-47891 Aalto XML processor ignores maxInMemorySize -- needs WebFlux + the Aalto async XML parser. No WebFlux; no aalto/Aalto on any classpath. CVE-2026-47892 WebFlux functional endpoints on DispatcherServlet, pre-flight header predicate bypass -- needs WebFlux functional endpoints. None exist. CVE-2026-47893 WebFlux WebSocket exception leaks request headers -- needs a WebFlux WebSocket application. The eight Boot 3.5 services are servlet-stack; the gateway proxies WebSocket frames but runs no WebFlux WS handler. CVE-2026-59280 FreeMarker + SpringTemplateLoader path traversal from an untrusted view name -- no FreeMarker on any classpath, no SpringTemplateLoader. CVE-2026-59281 Reflected XSS via the no-argument Errors.getFieldErrors() / getFieldError() accessors during server-side form rendering -- MAS is a JSON REST API consumed by an Angular SPA; zero server-side form or error-tag rendering, zero getFieldError(s)() call sites. CVE-2026-59282 Data-binding DoS via user-supplied nested property paths -- MAS binds request bodies as JSON through Jackson (@RequestBody), not through WebDataBinder onto nested Java-bean property paths; no @ModelAttribute form binding on untrusted nested paths. CVE-2026-59283 SpEL SimpleEvaluationContext safety-guard bypass when the SpEL compiler is active -- no dynamic SpEL evaluation, no SimpleEvaluation Context, no spring.expression.compiler.mode set. CVE-2026-59313 SSE stream corruption -- same requirements as CVE-2026-47890. CVE-2026-59314 ContentDisposition response splitting -- blocked by the Tomcat connector (rejects CR/LF in header values per the advisory), and the three ContentDisposition call sites in the estate (mas-backend-masters PublicWebsiteController, mas-file-upload DocumentController, MiningLease RenewalEnvironmentalClearanceController) all use the filename(name, Charset) overload, which emits the RFC 5987 filename* form and percent-encodes CR/LF regardless of Spring version.
Scoped to spring-core 6.2.x by file path on purpose: the rule stops matching the moment a service moves to the Boot 4 / spring-core 7.0.9+ line, so it expires by itself rather than masking a future finding. RE-REVIEW the grep list above each round.

NOT APPLICABLE / NO OSS FIX AVAILABLE. CVE-2026-59284: Spring Cloud Commons applies no allow-list to property keys when the WRITABLE /actuator/env endpoint is enabled (POST /actuator/env). Affects spring-cloud-commons 4.3.0 - 4.3.3 (fixed 4.3.4) and 5.0.0 - 5.0.2 (fixed 5.0.3). Dependency-Check attaches it to both spring-cloud-commons and spring-cloud-context.
Only mas-api-gateway ships spring-cloud-commons; this rule is a no-op safety net in the other repos. The gateway is not exposed: - management.endpoints.web.exposure.include is "health" (prod) / "health,info" (default) -- the env endpoint is not exposed at all, read or write. - the writable variant additionally needs management.endpoint.env.post.enabled=true, which is false by default and is not set anywhere. - actuator listens on management.server.port 9080, and no Kubernetes Service maps that port, so nothing outside the pod can reach any actuator endpoint. - the CVE also requires PR:H (an already-authenticated high-privilege caller).
No OSS fix for the 4.3.x line: 4.3.3 is the last spring-cloud-commons 4.3.x on Maven Central (verified against repo1.maven.org), 4.3.4 is Enterprise Support Only. The OSS fix is 5.0.3, which ships in Spring Cloud 2025.1.x on Spring Boot 4 -- same migration as the spring-core entry above. Scoped to the 4.x file path so it expires on the move to spring-cloud-commons 5.x.
